question.text:
Consider the Merge Sort algorithm applied to an array of size $n$.

Suppose every time we divide the array, instead of splitting it exactly in half, the left subarray always has $\left\lceil\frac{9 n}{10}\right\rceil$ elements and the right subarray has the rest.

Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding this algorithm?

  1. The recurrence relation for this algorithm is: $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{n})=\mathrm{T}\left(\frac{9 n}{10}\right)+\mathrm{T}\left(\frac{n}{10}\right)+\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{n})$
     
  2. The worst-case time complexity of this algorithm is $O(n \log n)$ where $O$ represents big-oh
     
  3. The worst-case time complexity of this algorithm is $\theta($ nlogn $)$ where $\theta$ represents big-theta
     
  4. The worst-case time complexity of this algorithm is $\theta\left(n^2\right)$ where $\theta$ represents big-theta

question.text:
LazySort(A):
    n = length(A)

    if n = 0 or n = 1:
        return A

    pivot = A[1]                 # always pick the first element
    left  = LazySort(elements < pivot)   // apply recursion on elements smaller than pivot
    right = LazySort(elements > pivot)   // apply recursion on elements greater than pivot

    B = left + [pivot] + right   # concatenate
    return MergeSort(B)          # finally call MergeSort

What is the tightest upper bound of this algorithm?

(Here $\Theta$ represents big-theta.)

  1. $\Theta\left(n \log ^2 n\right)$
     
  2. $\Theta\left(n^2 \log n\right)$
     
  3. $\Theta\left(n^3\right) \mathrm{}$
     
  4. $\Theta\left(n^2 \log n\right)$
